subject: Political Science
central_question: How can democratic societies turn formal membership into full and equal citizenship while addressing migration, inequality, diversity, refugees and global interdependence?
in_scope_units: Introduction to citizenship as full and equal membership, rights, identity and obligations.
Full and Equal Membership through movement, migration, insider–outsider conflicts and democratic dispute resolution.
Equal Rights through the urban poor, T. H. Marshall, livelihood, shelter and group-specific needs.
Citizen and Nation through inclusive national identity and India’s constitutional experiment.
Universal Citizenship and Global Citizenship through refugees, statelessness and cross-border cooperation.
banned_topics: Detailed theories of national self-determination, which belong to Nationalism.
Detailed categories and moral origins of rights, which belong to Rights.
Detailed secular-state models and religious equality, which belong to Secularism.

known_pitfalls.claim: Citizenship is only a legal document or nationality label.
known_pitfalls.correction: It includes full and equal membership, rights, identity, protection and obligations towards others.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every citizen can exercise equal rights equally once law grants them.
known_pitfalls.correction: Poverty, insecure housing, discrimination and lack of resources can obstruct actual exercise.

known_pitfalls.claim: Migrants contribute nothing and only consume local resources.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter describes their labour and skills across technology, nursing, construction, services and small enterprise.

known_pitfalls.claim: Inclusive national identity requires everyone to abandon cultural differences.
known_pitfalls.correction: India’s constitutional project combines common political membership with protection of language, religion and culture.

known_pitfalls.claim: Global citizenship has already replaced state citizenship.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is an emerging idea that may supplement national citizenship and support cooperation and basic protection.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Exercise Q1 on rights and obligations of citizenship.
Use NCERT Exercise Q5 to analyse migration and local contribution.
Use NCERT Exercise Q2 to distinguish legal rights from their effective exercise.
Use NCERT Exercise Q6 to explain citizenship as an ongoing project.
Conclude with NCERT Exercise Q4 on refugees and global citizenship.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises contain Questions 1–6 on rights and obligations, equal exercise, citizenship struggles, refugees, migration and democratic citizenship as a project.
